title: Geological CO2 storage permanence verification
bottleneck: Injected CO2 must stay underground for millennia to count as removal, but verifying permanence is unsolved: monitoring wells sample tiny fractions of a plume, old abandoned wells can leak, and induced seismicity can open new pathways. Mineralization in basalt is fast and secure but geographically limited; saline aquifers are vast but rely on caprock integrity over geological timescales no institution can guarantee. Leakage accounting rules are still being written.
why_it_blocks: Without credible permanence verification, stored CO2 is an accounting fiction — credits get sold for carbon that may return to the atmosphere. The uncertainty blocks both financing and public acceptance of the storage leg of every CDR pathway.
current_state: Projects like Carbfix in Iceland demonstrate rapid basalt mineralization at small scale, and the US has permitted large saline-aquifer storage hubs. But long-term monitoring standards, liability rules, and leakage detection at the required sensitivity are still under development.
